1About this guide

You are the focal person of a Business Unit (BU) in the Africa CDC Results-Based Management (RBM) platform. This guide shows everything you do there, in the order you do it:

  1. Plan the specific activities of your BU and send them for approval.
  2. Follow each activity until it is approved, and fix it when it is rejected.
  3. Report on what the activities delivered (activity reports) and on the results of your indicators (the quarterly indicator report).

Your activities and reports are approved by the Responsible Person of the Business Unit (usually the head of division or director), called the Responsible Person in this guide: the person named for your BU in the org structure. The M&E team then follows the results. Each of them has their own guide.

A specific activity is a concrete piece of work under a broad activity of your BU: a mission, a training, a workshop, a procurement.

The guide follows the platform as it works on 7 November 2026. The screen captures come from the platform itself, filled with sample data: names, activities and amounts are examples.

The menu and the buttons you see depend on your permissions. If a colleague sees an item you do not, that is expected.

Where to find this guide

In the platform, click User guides, the last entry of the main menu. The page lists the guide of each role: Open reads it in the browser, Download saves the PDF.

Help, at the right end of the main menu, opens this guide in a new tab on the chapter about the page you are on. On a phone it is at the top of the menu: Help on this page.

The tour

The first time you sign in, a short tour of the screen opens on your home page. Each step points at a part of the screen and says what it is for. Click Next and Back to move from step to step. Skip the tour, or the Escape key, closes it. To take it again, click your initials at the top right, then Take the tour.

2Signing in and finding your way

Open the platform in your browser and click Sign in with Microsoft, with your Africa CDC account, the same one as Outlook and Teams. There is no separate password for the platform.

If your session ends, the sign-in screen says so. Sign in again: the platform takes you back to the page you were on. Your work is saved on the server, so you never lose what you saved.

If the screen says No RBM account matches this Microsoft account, check that you chose your Africa CDC account in the Microsoft window, or select Request access to write to the RBM team (pra@africacdc.org). Under the button, Need help? opens the user guides and the RBM team contact, even before you sign in.

The top menu

Three items are dropdowns: Aggregates (what your Business Unit has: workplan, PIRS, budget), Activities (planning and activity reports) and Indicators (indicators and the quarterly indicator report). Click the item, then the page you want.

Top menuItemWhat it opens
DashboardYour home page: the progress of your Business Unit. It opens on a year that has started.
Aggregates ▾WorkplanThe workplan of your Business Unit for the selected year.
PIRSThe indicators of your Business Unit, as in the PIRS (Performance Indicator Reference Sheets).
Project ProposalThe project proposal. Only if your role can read the plans.
Budget OverviewThe budget codes of the broad activities of your Business Unit.
Activities ▾Broad ActivitiesThe broad activities your Business Unit is responsible for.
Specific ActivitiesYour specific activities, their status and their actions (chapter 6). The New specific button opens a blank form (chapter 4).
Write Activity ReportsReport on what an approved activity delivered (chapter 7).
Indicators ▾T3 / T4 IndicatorsThe Tier 3 and Tier 4 indicators of your Business Unit.
Write Indicator ReportThe quarterly indicator report: the result of each indicator (chapter 8).
Country WorkplanActivities planned in your country (chapter 9). Members of a country office only.
Reporting ▾Big Tickets, the quarterly dashboard and donor reports.
User guidesThe guide of each role, to read in the browser or download as PDF (chapter 1).

Approvers also see Approve Activity Reports, Approve Indicator Reports and Review Submissions.

Two roles? If you also hold an administrator role, your pages as a focal person are gathered in one dropdown called BU, next to the administration menus. It lists the same pages one by one.

The BU selector

If you belong to several Business Units, the BU selector on the right of the top bar chooses the BU you work on: one BU, or All my divisions. It decides which broad activities the form offers you and what the lists, the PIRS and the Budget Overview show. It is hidden when you belong to one BU only. If you belong to a country office, pick the office here to plan its activities (chapter 4).

The year selector

Next to it, the year selector chooses the fiscal year. A year that has not started carries the label PLANNING and, in the list, Not started, planning only. Your choice is kept in your browser and in the page address (?fy=2027).

  • Planning pages follow the year. The pages of Aggregates, Broad Activities, Specific Activities, the form, T3 / T4 Indicators and the Country Workplan show the selected year. A new activity is created in that year.
  • Reporting pages need a year that has started. On a future year, the Dashboard, Write Activity Reports and Write Indicator Report show “FY2027 has not started” with a Switch to FY2026 button.

3Before you plan

Check the BU and the year of the top bar (for the 2027 workplan: FY 2027), then look at what your activity will hang on.

Your broad activities

Open Activities › Broad Activities. The page lists the broad activities your BU is responsible for in the selected year, with their code, title and budget. Click a row to open one.

The FY2027 broad activities come from the AMERT 2027 budget proposal, with codes such as 2.1.1.01. A 2027 code can hold another activity than in 2026: check that the year selector reads FY 2027 before you plan. Your 2026 specific activities are not copied into 2027 by themselves; you can copy one with Copy to 2027 (chapter 6). A broad activity is missing? It belongs to another BU, or it is not in the plan of that year: contact the PR&A team.

Your T3/T4 indicators

Open Indicators › T3 / T4 Indicators. The FY2027 Tier 3 and Tier 4 indicators come from the PIRS version 7.0, with codes such as SDI.2.1-3. You will link your activity to one of them.

The annual targets of every Tier 3 and Tier 4 indicator are set in the PIRS. As the focal person of your BU, you review them with the other staff of your division and get the approval of the head of division. If something is inconsistent, contact the M&E team to discuss it and make the corrections. The quarterly targets entered for your BU decide in which quarters a report is expected: a quarter with a target above 0 expects one.

Have this ready

  • The broad activity and, if relevant, the indicator it serves.
  • The activity and mission type and the place or places where it happens.
  • The focal person of the activity, a staff member of your BU.
  • The funding source and the cost of each expense (tickets, DSA, venue, materials).

4Creating a specific activity

Open Activities › Specific Activities and click New specific. The form opens in the year of the year selector. It has four sections, in this order: Activity information, Location, Funding & Budget and Decision Complexity Screening. Fields marked * are required.

Step 1: Activity information

Choose the broad activity first.

  • Parent Broad Activity *: the list holds only the broad activities your BU is responsible for: the BU chosen in the BU selector, or all your BUs when All my divisions is chosen.
  • Linked Indicator (T3/T4): optional. The list holds the T3/T4 indicators of the Business Unit of the broad activity you chose; if it has none, those of your own BUs. When you change the broad activity, the indicator is cleared: pick it again.
  • Budget code (from the broad activity): shown under the broad activity once you choose it, for information. These are the budget codes of the broad activity; you do not choose one. The activity page shows them too.
  • Specific Activity name *: a short, clear name. With several places (Step 2) the platform adds the place to the name.
  • Description: one or two sentences. It pre-fills the objectives of your activity reports later.
  • Activity and mission type *: one of the seven types of the Activity Reporting Template: I. Official engagement, II. Training, III. Event (workshop, meeting, conference), IV. Procurement, V. In-office, VI. Recruitment & HR, VII. Others. Your activity reports take this type: you do not choose it again when you report.
  • Implementation at RCC *: Yes if a Regional Coordinating Centre carries out the activity, No otherwise.
  • Is this an operational activity?: optional, Yes or No.
  • Risk level: optional. High, Medium or Low: how likely the activity is to be delayed or not delivered. It shows on the activity page and in your list, where the riskiest activities come first (chapter 6). When the risk level is High and the activity is approved or in review, the focal person of the activity and the Responsible Person receive an email, A high-risk activity starts soon, when its start date is 14 days away or less, so they can check that the risk is still managed. It is sent once per start date.
  • Secondary responsible divisions/units: optional, as many as needed. A label only: it gives these Business Units no access and no approval step.
  • Focal person (staff of the division) *: a staff member of your BU. It is needed to submit; a draft can be saved without it.

The form has no start or end date. The actual dates are recorded later, in the activity report.

Step 2: Location

The location is optional and hidden when the type is IV. Procurement. Click Add a place and pick Addis Ababa (HQ), Virtual (remote) or any country of the world.

Several places mean several activities. With more than one place, saving creates one activity per place, each named after the activity and its place. Each one has its own cost lines, budget, approval and reports.

  • The quarterly cost breakdown you type applies to the first place. The other places start with a breakdown of 0: complete them later by editing each one.
  • All of them get the same complexity screening answers, and they are submitted together.
  • If one place cannot be created, a message names it and the others are kept.

Step 3: Funding & Budget

  • Budgeting arrangement *: Extramural or Intramural.
  • Primary funding source * and Other funding source: pick from the list or type a new value. Grant name: optional.
  • Total cost of activity (USD) *: required. Enter 0 for an activity with no cost; an empty field counts as missing. With several places the field is replaced by the total of each place's cost lines.
  • Quarterly cost breakdown (USD): the cost in each quarter of the year. If the four quarters do not add up to the total, an amber message warns you; you can still save.
  • Cost breakdown by expense category (USD): click Add a cost line for each expense, choose the expense category (Travel Ticket, Travel DSA, Conference Facilities…), describe it and enter the amount. The platform adds up the lines.
  • When the lines and the total cost differ (one place): an amber message shows the gap and offers a button that copies the lines total into the total cost. For example, you typed a total cost of 10,000 and your cost lines add up to 9,500. The message reads The lines add up to $9,500, the total cost of the activity is $10,000. Click Use $9,500 as total cost: the total cost becomes 9,500. If the total cost is right, correct the lines instead. The message is a warning: it does not stop you from saving.
  • With several places, a Place column appears: give each line its place. Every place needs at least one priced line.

The budget of the year. The total cost is the budget of the activity for the year it is planned in. On the activity page the boxes are labelled Total 2026, Budget 2027 and Budget 2028: they are the plan year and the two years after it, so for an FY2027 activity Total 2026 shows the 2027 budget.

Step 4: Decision Complexity Screening

Answer “Does the implementation of this planned activity require complex decision-making?” with Yes or No. The answer is required. On Yes, rate five criteria from Low to High: Information Requirements, Stakeholder Involvement, Scope & Impact, Process Steps & Timeframe, and Risk & Uncertainty. The platform adds up a score from 5 to 15 and shows the band: 5 to 7 lower complexity, 8 to 11 moderate, 12 to 15 high.

The screening is for planning support only. It does not change the approval of the activity.

Step 5: Required fields and messages

Both save buttons stay disabled until the required fields are filled. Once the name and the broad activity are in, an amber line above the buttons lists what is still missing.

NeededSectionBefore you can
Parent Broad ActivityActivity informationSave
Specific Activity nameActivity informationSave
Activity and mission typeActivity informationSave
Implementation at RCC (Yes or No)Activity informationSave
Focal person (staff of the division)Activity informationSubmit
Budgeting arrangementFunding & BudgetSave
Primary funding sourceFunding & BudgetSave
Total cost of activity (0 is accepted, empty is not)Funding & BudgetSave
A category and a description on every cost lineFunding & BudgetSave
Several places: a place on every cost line, and cost lines for every placeFunding & BudgetSave
The Yes / No answer to the complexity question, and on Yes the five ratingsDecision Complexity ScreeningSave

MessageWhat to do

Planning for a country office

If you are a member of an Africa CDC country office, pick the office in the BU selector before you open the form. Then:

  • The Parent Broad Activity list offers every broad activity of the year: a country office has no broad activity of its own. The T3/T4 offered are those of the chosen broad activity's Business Unit.
  • The activity is carried by the country office, and its location is already set to the office's country. You can change it.
  • The Focal person list holds the staff of the office.
  • The Responsible Person of the country office approves it, and once submitted it appears in the Country Workplan of that country (chapter 9).

5Save as a draft, or submit

At the bottom of the form:

  • Save draft keeps the activity as a Draft. Drafts stay private until you submit. Come back to it from Activities › Specific Activities.
  • Save & submit for approval saves it and sends it to the Responsible Person. The message reads Submitted for approval and the status becomes In Review.
  • Cancel leaves the form without saving.

You then return to Activities › Specific Activities. With several places, a second message confirms the other activities, for example “1 more activity created: Uganda”.

What happens after you submit

  • The Responsible Person of your Business Unit receives an email with a link to the activity, and finds it in their review list.
  • If your BU has no Responsible Person named, the Responsible Person of the Business Unit above it decides.
  • When they decide, you receive an email with the decision, the reason when it is a rejection, and a link to the activity.

The life of a specific activity

StatusWhat it means
DraftSaved but not submitted. Drafts stay private until you submit. Everything can still change.
In ReviewSubmitted. The Responsible Person of the Business Unit decides. It cannot be edited from the list while it waits.
ApprovedPart of the workplan of the Business Unit. It shows in the Workplan and, if its place is a country with a country office, in the Country Workplan.
RejectedSent back with a reason. Edit it and submit it again.
CancelledWithdrawn from the workplan. It stays in the list for the record.

6Following your activities

The Specific Activities page

Open Activities › Specific Activities. The page shows the activities of your BU for the selected year, including your drafts, your activities in review and the rejected ones. A rejected activity shows the reason on a red line under its row, and the risk level shows as a chip next to the title.

The order. The activities that need your action come first: rejected (to fix and submit again), then drafts (to submit), then in review, approved and cancelled. Within each status, the riskiest come first (High, Medium, Low, then not assessed), then the latest change.

The filters. Narrow the list with the status tabs (All, Drafts, In review, Approved, Rejected, Cancelled), the search box, and the Type, Funding source, Budgeting arrangement and Risk lists. Clear filters removes them. The filters are kept in the page address: copy it to share the filtered list with a colleague.

Each row has an Actions menu: View details; Edit and Submit for approval on drafts and rejected activities; Flag ownership dispute if the activity does not belong to your BU; Delete draft or Cancel activity.

An activity In Review cannot be edited from the list while it waits for the decision. The bell in the top bar also lists the activities you created that were rejected, with the reason.

The Approval trail

Click the code or the title of an activity to open its page. At the bottom, the section Approval trail lists what happened to the activity, oldest first: the date, the person and the event.

EventMeaning
Created as draftThe activity was first saved.
EditedSomeone saved a change. Several saves in a row by the same person show as one line.
Submitted for approvalIt was sent to the Responsible Person.
ApprovedThe Responsible Person approved it.
RejectedThe Responsible Person sent it back. Their reason shows in quotes under the line.
Edited, sent back for approvalAn approved activity was changed, so it went back to review.
CancelledThe activity was withdrawn from the workplan.

While the activity is In Review, a line at the top says whom it waits for, for example Waiting for: Responsible Person A (Responsible Person of the Business Unit). If it reads Waiting for: nobody: ask your administrator to name one in Org Structure, nobody can approve it yet: tell the PR&A team.

A rejected activity

  1. Read the reason: in the decision email, on the red line in the list, or in the Approval trail.
  2. Open Actions › Edit and correct the activity.
  3. Click Save & submit for approval. Or save it, then use Actions › Submit for approval. It goes back to In Review.

After approval

An Approved activity is part of the workplan of your BU: Aggregates › Workplan shows it under its broad activity, and it counts in the Gantt chart and the dashboards. Its page shows everything that was planned, including the Activity and Mission Type (for example II. Training), the Risk Level and the budget code of the broad activity, and the full trail.

If you save a change to an approved activity, it goes back to In Review by itself and the Responsible Person approves it again. For other changes to an approved plan (a broad activity, an indicator, a target, a budget you already report on), contact the PR&A team.

Deleting or cancelling

  • Delete draft (on a Draft): the activity is deleted for good, after a confirmation.
  • Cancel activity (any other status): the activity becomes Cancelled. It leaves the live workplan, any pending approval is closed, and it stays in your list for the record.

Copying an activity to the next year

To plan an activity again the next year, open Activities › Specific Activities on the year it was planned in, for example FY 2026. In the Actions menu of the activity, click Copy to 2027. The item shows only when the plan of the next year is in the platform.

The new-activity form opens on the next year, filled from the activity you copy: name, description, type, risk level, places, funding, total cost and quarters, cost lines and complexity screening. A note at the top names the activity it copies.

  • The Parent Broad Activity and the Linked Indicator (T3/T4) are left empty: their codes change from one year to the next, so pick those of the new year.
  • The dates are not copied.
  • Nothing is saved until you click Save draft or Save & submit for approval. The copy then follows the usual path: draft, review, approval. The activity you copied does not change.

7Writing activity reports

Once an activity is approved and its year has started, you report on what it delivered. Open Activities › Write Activity Reports.

Step 1: Check the quarter and find your activity

The page opens on the quarter whose reporting window is open, and a green line says so, for example “Activity reports written now count for Q3 2026, the open reporting window (open until Oct 30, 2026)”. Activities are grouped under their broad activity. Each row shows the code, the name, the budget, a status and an action button.

Can't see your activities? Reporting is open to any member of a division. If your activities don't appear, ask the Responsible Person of your BU to add you to its team. An activity planned in several places has one row per place.

Step 2: Open the report form

Click Report on an activity with no report yet, or New report to add one. Several reports on the same activity are allowed: each one carries its author's name, follows its own approval and never overwrites another. Click an existing report under the activity name to open it.

Step 3: Fill in the report

The form follows the official Africa CDC Activity Reporting Template, with the same item numbers.

ItemPart of the formWhat goes in
1, 2, 3, 5Background (from the workplan)Tier 2 outcome, output indicator, activity name and code, broad activity. Filled for you; you cannot change them here.
4Activity and mission typeThe type of the activity, chosen when it was created. Read-only, marked From the specific activity. To change it, edit the specific activity (an approved activity then goes back to review).
6Dates and durationStart and end date. The duration counts both days: a one-day workshop is 1 day.
7Location & venueHeadquarters, Remote / virtual or any country, and the exact venue.
8Organising staffLead organiser and other team members, picked from the staff list.
9Activity objectivesPre-filled from the description entered at planning, except for In-office and Others. Adjust if needed.
10a–10eActivity summaryParticipants and Member States covered, key strategic needs addressed (AHSS), narrative of key achievements, key challenges and recommendations, means of verification and files.
–Specific informationOnly for Official engagement, Event and Training (table below).
11Activity logisticsBudget code, filled from the broad activity, and the total cost used, which you enter from the actual spend.
–Sign-offPrepared by, approved by and submission date. Filled by the platform.

For three types, a Specific information section follows item 4:

Activity and mission typeExtra fields
Official engagementVisited entity, purpose of the visit, key issues discussed or observed, outputs or outcomes, recommendations and follow-up actions.
EventParticipating stakeholders, key discussions, outputs or outcomes of the meeting, follow-up actions.
TrainingDescription of the trainees, delivery methodology, number trained (total, of whom women, of whom men, other breakdowns), participants' evaluation and feedback, proposed improvements.

An older activity without a type shows Not set: choose it on the specific activity. at item 4. Edit the specific activity, choose its type, then come back to the report.

Not started yet? Tick This activity has not started yet at the top of the form and choose the quarter in which it is expected to start. That is the only required field: you can then submit without dates, location, narrative, spend or file.

Step 4: Attach your evidence

Under Verification Files, click + Upload file to attach proof: an attendance list, photos, a report (max 20 MB per file). Prefer PDF: Word, Excel and PowerPoint files are converted to PDF on upload. In a new report, save a draft first, then upload.

Step 5: Save or submit

  • Save draft keeps your work as a Draft.
  • Save & submit for approval sends it to the Responsible Person; the status becomes Submitted.

Submitting requires a start date and an end date, the location, the lead organiser, the narrative of key achievements (10c), the total cost used (11; enter 0 if nothing was spent) and at least one verification file. Until then a note next to the button lists what is missing. After you submit, the form becomes read-only. The author of a draft can remove it with Delete this draft.

The life of a report

StatusWhat it means
Not startedNo report has been opened for this activity or indicator yet.
DraftStarted and saved, not yet submitted.
SubmittedSubmitted. It waits for the decision of the reviewer.
In reviewAn indicator or activity report on its way through its approval steps.
ApprovedAccepted. It now counts in the dashboards and exports.
RejectedSent back with a reason. Fix it and submit it again.
N/AMarked “not applicable”: no report is expected for this item this quarter.

The Responsible Person of your BU approves or rejects your activity reports. You receive an email with the decision and, for a rejection, the reason: fix the report and submit it again. Only approved reports count in the dashboards.

8Writing the quarterly indicator report

Each quarter, your BU writes the quarterly indicator report: the result of each Tier 3 or Tier 4 indicator. Open Indicators › Write Indicator Report.

Step 1: Pick the quarter

Choose the quarter tab. You can submit only while the quarter's window is open; a banner says if it is open or closed. When it is closed you can still view past reports, but not change them.

Step 2: Open the indicator report

Each row is one indicator, with its tier, your role (Main or Contributor), the baseline and targets, the actual value and the status. In the Action column click Report (new), Edit (draft or rejected) or View (submitted). The ⋮ menu also offers Open report, Contributors and Copy link; on Main rows it offers Mark as not applicable for a quarter with no result to report.

Step 3: Fill in the report

  • Results Achieved: the number or percentage reached this quarter. Required to submit.
  • Narrations of Performance (Key Milestones): the story behind the number. Write a full description in complete sentences, not a one-line bullet.
  • Challenges and Recommendations: add as many as needed with + Add. Link each challenge to the activities you carried out; each recommendation answers a challenge.
  • Verification Files: your means of verification.
  • Disaggregated Level Results: optional breakdowns (by sex, region…).

The activity reports behind the indicator

While you can edit the report, a green panel under the narrative lists the approved activity reports of the same quarter that feed this indicator: the activities of your Business Unit linked to the indicator, on the specific activity form or through their broad activity. Each line shows the code and the name of the activity and what it achieved. Click the code to open the activity report.

Add to the narrative copies these lines at the end of Narrations of Performance. Turn them into full sentences, then save: nothing is saved until you save. The panel does not fill Results Achieved: enter the number yourself. Activity reports declared not started are not listed, and the panel does not show when no approved activity report matches.

Step 4: Save or submit

Use Save Draft to keep working (the form also saves your draft every few seconds), or Submit Report to send it. Submit stays disabled until Results Achieved has a value.

Who approves it depends on your role on the indicator. A report of the Main BU goes to M&E for sign-off. A report of a Contributing BU is reviewed by the Responsible Person of your BU, then by the Responsible Person of the main BU, then signed off by M&E. The Workflow Timeline at the bottom of the form shows each step and whom it waits for.

9Country Workplan

If you are a member of an Africa CDC country office, the top menu shows Country Workplan. It lists every specific activity located in your country for the selected year, whatever the Business Unit that plans it.

  • Only countries that have a country office have a Country Workplan.
  • It shows the activities whose location is exactly the country and whose status is Approved, In Execution, Closed or In Review. Drafts never appear.
  • Each row shows the code and name, the Business Unit, the focal person, the dates, the budget and the status, 15 rows per page. Click a row to open the activity.
  • Activities planned in the form have no dates yet: the column shows a dash.
  • The activities a country office plans for itself (chapter 4) appear here once submitted.

Need help? You plan and report yourself. For any change to a broad activity (name, code, budget), an indicator (name, baseline, target), the reporting timeline, the org structure, or the budget of an activity you already report on, contact the PR&A team. For the platform, contact the Software Developer Unit. This guide reflects the platform as configured on 7 November 2026; screens evolve as it is improved.
